text:
Maya: Quick proposal — we need a safer way to grant temporary per-API-key scaling for internal services/partners that ties to live telemetry and auto-rolls back. Current one-off top-ups are too manual and create billing/audit gaps. Thoughts?

Liam: +1. Can you sketch what "graduated" means here? like linear ramp, bins, or reactive?

Maya: Thinking of a small state machine: initial spike allowance -> elevated steady-state -> auto-decay back to baseline. Each stage has hard limits, TTLs, and a telemetry trigger (p95 error, queue depth, or cost threshold) to move between stages. Also must be auditable and only available for internal/partner keys.

Avery: Sounds good. We should expose via both Console and an admin API. Console UX: a single flow to start an override with previewed cost delta + suggested telemetry triggers. Example UI copy: "Grant temporary multiplier to key svc-analytics (3h) — estimated +$120 — auto-revert on low latency or after 3h"

Sasha: Security question — who can escalate a key? We need RBAC: devops on-call vs. partner-eng vs engineering. Also require an "approval-required" flag for production-critical orgs. Plus KMS auth for any change to key config.

Rory: From runtime side, we need to implement a small token flag that the routing layer checks to bypass per-key soft caps and use a controlled multiplier. Important: keep circuit-breaker so the override doesn't allow full resource exhaustion. e.g., override gives multiplier up to X but still respects cluster-wide capacity caps.

Liam: Billing impact: we must surface estimated token and GPU-cost delta before approving. Also ensure we emit a billing tag so downstream billing pipeline can attribute incremental usage to the override (labels: override_id, request_origin).

Maya: Agreed. Proposal for admin API/CLI shape: a single endpoint to create a "KeyOverride" object with fields: key_id, stages (array), max_multiplier, ttl, approval_required, rollback_policy. Example CLI: 
```
rdwctl quotas override create \n  --key=svc-analytics \n  --stages="spike:5m@5x,elevated:3h@2x" \n  --max-multiplier=5 \n  --ttl=3h \n  --approval=oncall \n  --rollback=auto-on-cost-threshold:200
```

Rory: Nice. On the routing layer we can implement multiplier as a post-rate-limit weight adjustment so we don't change core token-bucket math. That helps keep p99 predictable. We'll also require a per-key heap of KV cache capacity so per-request latency isn't impacted by sudden bursts.

quota-bot: proposed_override_preview: {"key":"svc-analytics","est_tokens":42000,"est_cost_usd":"$120","override_id":"ovr-1965432100-1","required_approvals":["oncall"]} (this is a simulation)

Avery: For Console, show a timeline view: requested -> active -> decaying -> expired/rolled-back. Allow manual extend/override if approver present. Also show live telemetry: p50/p95 cost/token, backend errors, queue length.

Sasha: Audit trail must include who requested, who approved, timestamps, reasoning, and the full override payload. Also store a signed snapshot to S3 for compliance. Example audit record (stringified in logs): 
```
OVERRIDE_LOG|ovr-1965432100-1|requester=Maya|approver=Liam|key=svc-analytics|stages=spike(5m,5x)->elevated(3h,2x)|cost_est=$120|ts=1965432100
```

Maya: Telemetry hooks: we need two things — (1) a streaming signal from runtime that counts "override delta tokens" per minute, and (2) a periodic job that evaluates rollback triggers (cost breach, sustained error rate). We'll also emit metrics per override_id for tracing and dashboards.

Liam: Ops concerns: if partner traffic is legitimately different, we should allow pinned rollouts (longer TTL) but require finance pre-approval. Also consider a quota-exempt mode for internal infra keys with special limits but still logged.

Rory: Implementation plan (runtime): 1) add override API and store in config DB 2) runtime pulls override + multiplier, applies to per-key limiter 3) add soft safety cap computed from cluster capacity 4) emit override_id tags on requests 5) backfill dashboards. I can do POC for step 2/3 next sprint.

Avery: Console work: wire up Create Override modal to admin API, show cost preview from pricing service, and add timeline + cancel button. UX estimate: 2 weeks.

Sasha: Security tasks: add RBAC check in admin API, require 2FA for approvers for >24h overrides, and require an approval reason. Compliance will need export of audit_log for SOC.

Maya: Open questions:
- Should we allow conditional overrides triggered by workload signals automatically (no human in loop)? e.g., if p95 latency > 1.2s, promote to elevated stage.
- How granular are stages? fixed buckets vs percentiles?
- Do we allow partner self-service for some tiers?

Liam: I vote for human-in-the-loop by default, with a toggle to allow "auto-trigger" for trusted partner keys (opt-in, audited).

Rory: For stage granularity: implement bucketed stages for now (spike/elevated/steady). Simpler and safer.

Maya: Action items:
- Rory: POC runtime multiplier + soft cap (next sprint)
- Avery: Console mockups + cost preview API contract (EOW)
- Sasha: RBAC + 2FA requirement spec (EOW)
- Liam: Billing tag spec and estimator inputs (EOW)
- Maya: Draft admin API schema and example CLI (I'll post RFC)

Avery: I'll mock the modal and timeline and drop screenshots here when ready.

quota-bot: reminder: any override >24h requires at least 2 approvers per policy POL-OVERRIDE-2025

Maya: Thanks all. I'll open an RFC and link it here. If anyone has objections to the staged auto-decay approach speak up now, otherwise I'll move forward with the RFC and include the POC timelines. :+1:
